findings.evidence: In fieldProofComposition.fields, s0168-idiomatic (from frozen-English-a, reviewer 0f487fa0) changes 'I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.' to 'I have lived in your country for a long time, and I am loath to kill you.' The source unit is the extant 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝. 恨不+verb means 'regret not', and 'loath to kill you' is the Tongjian variant 恨恨不欲殺汝 (or the Yulan 誓不殺汝 sense), not a reading of the extant text. The field's own sourceReason (also productionReasons s0168/en) says not to treat 恨不 as simply reluctant and not to silently emend. The applied s0168-literal-English-note, by contrast, keeps 'I regret not killing you' and flags the variant explicitly. Applying both would install contradictory, unmarked renderings of one sentence.
